sources.note: Guachi (abbrev. GCI) appears only in comparative lexical tables (e.g. 'GCI aati' 'estrela', 'GCI leek' 'terra') and in the Macro-Mataguayo-Guaykuru tree (p. 793). Nothing on stress.

sources.citation: Campbell, Lyle. 2012. Classification of the indigenous languages of South America. In Lyle Campbell & Verónica Grondona (eds.), The indigenous languages of South America: a comprehensive guide, 59-166 (Guachí pp. 69, 90); and Campbell & Grondona, Languages of the Chaco and Southern Cone, p. 626. Berlin: De Gruyter Mouton.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Classification only: 'Guachí is an extinct language of Brazil, often associated with Guaicuruan. Perhaps it should be placed rather in section 5, unclassified extinct languages' (p. 69); 'Guachí (Brazil) and Payaguá (Paraguay), both extinct, are often attributed to Guaicuruan, but the evidence for this remains unclear. (See Viegas Barros 2004.)' (p. 90). Nothing on phonology or stress.

sources.citation: Fabre, Alain. 2005 [last modified 2021-03-12]. Diccionario etnolingüístico y guía bibliográfica de los pueblos indígenas sudamericanos: GUAYKURÚ (update of Suplemento Antropológico 41/2 (2006): 7-132, Asunción).
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Bibliographic survey; Guachí only in classification discussion ('Como las dos últimas lenguas [payaguá, guachí] son escasamente documentadas..') and in the bibliography, which adds Moutinho 1869 ('Linguagem dos Guachis': pp. 141-142) and Viegas Barros 2004 (formerly hosted on the Etnolingüística Yahoo-group Biblioteca Virtual). Nothing on stress.

sources.citation: Martius, Carl Friedrich Philipp von. 1867. Beiträge zur Ethnographie und Sprachenkunde Amerika's zumal Brasiliens. II. Zur Sprachenkunde (Wörtersammlung brasilianischer Sprachen). Leipzig: Friedrich Fleischer. 'Guachis', pp. 131-133.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Latin-glossed alphabetical reprint of Castelnau's list ('*) Castelnau Expédit. V. 278') with a short comparative note ('Es unterliegt keinem Zweifel, dass die Sprache der Guachis demselben Stamme mit jener der Mbocobi oder Toba angehört'). Nothing on stress or pronunciation.

sources.citation: Castelnau, Francis de. 1851. Expédition dans les parties centrales de l'Amérique du Sud, de Rio de Janeiro à Lima, et de Lima au Para. Histoire du voyage, tome V. Paris: P. Bertrand. Appendice, 'IXe vocabulaire. Langue des Guachis (Environs de Miranda)', pp. 278-280.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: The sole primary record: c. 145 French-gloss/Guachi word pairs in French orthography (e.g. 'Dieu — Yathlein', 'Eau — Euak', 'Un — Tamak'). No accent marks used for stress, no pronunciation note except 'Soleil — O-es (ô long)'. Nothing on stress.

No descriptive reference at all; only classification notes citing Viegas Barros 2004, Montaño Aragón 1989, and the historical sources Castelnau 1851, Martius 1867, Koch-Grünberg 1902. 'Poorly attested extinct language of Southern Brazil of uncertain affiliation.'

State that the language is known only from 145 words collected by Castelnau in March-April 1845 near Miranda; no phonology section; references Castelnau 1851, Viegas Barros 2004, Campbell 2012, Loukotka 1968, Jolkesky 2016.
